summary.intent: Add all missing facet data (scores, stats, files touched, tool usage, implementation rationale, tradeoffs, codebase patterns, and all facet evidence fields) to the summary TUI detail pane, which currently shows only a subset of available session data.
summary.outcome: Design was fully decided (flat scroll, compact grouped layout with 4 boxes: SUMMARY, CODE, LEARNINGS, SIGNALS), spec was written and saved, implementation plan was created with 6 tasks, and subagent-driven execution was initiated starting with Task 1 (formatDuration helper).

repo: The insights.db SQLite database has 16 tables: sessions, tool_calls, files_touched, learnings, friction, codebase_patterns, implementation_rationale, tradeoffs, review_rule_signals, missing_context_signals, repeated_user_instructions, failure_loops, skill_signals, suggestions, cache_meta.

Facets backfilling works by: sessions are initially cached with has_facets=0, then on improve/insights/memory-loop runs the system extracts facets via LLM from condensed transcripts and writes results into facet tables, then marks has_facets=1.
The summary TUI detail pane is implemented in cmd/entire/cli/summarytui/detail_page.go.

SessionRow struct has many fields not rendered in the detail pane: InputTokens, CacheTokens, OutputTokens, APICallCount, DurationMs, AgentPct, OverallScore, ScoreTokenEff, ScoreFirstPass, ScoreFriction, ScoreFocus, FilesTouched, ImplementationRationale, Tradeoffs, CodebasePatterns, ToolCounts, and per-facet evidence fields.

Facet types are defined in cmd/entire/cli/facets/facets.go and include: friction, failure loops, repeated user instructions, missing context signals, skill signals, review rule signals, repo gotchas, workflow gaps.
The Codex companion adversarial review script fails with ENOBUFS on large repos due to buffer overflow when collecting git diff.

code.finding: Current detail pane has SUMMARY, FRICTION, LEARNINGS, and INSIGHTS boxes; INSIGHTS lumps all facet types into one flat list.

Facet structs include evidence fields: evidence strings on repeated instructions, missing context, failure loops; Friction and MissingInstruction on skill signals; Evidence, SourceKind, Strength, WhyReusable on review rule signals.

Subagent-driven development was chosen over inline execution for this task.

implementation_rationale: Flat scroll chosen over tabs or collapsible sections for simplicity — no hidden state, consistent with existing TUI paradigm.
Compact grouped layout (4 boxes) chosen over 17 separate boxes or hybrid header approach — groups related data without excessive visual noise.
LEARNINGS kept as its own box separate from SIGNALS because it comes from the summary phase, not the facet extraction phase.
Empty sub-sections and empty boxes are omitted entirely to avoid cluttering sparse sessions.
Scores and stats are placed inside the SUMMARY box (not a separate box) to keep quick-glance metadata together.
tradeoffs: Flat scroll vs tabbed sections: flat scroll is simpler but requires more scrolling for data-heavy sessions; tabs reduce scrolling but hide data.
Separate boxes per section (17 boxes) vs compact grouped layout (4 boxes): 17 boxes is maximally granular but visually overwhelming; 4 boxes trades granularity for readability.
Hybrid header (scores/stats always visible) vs compact grouped: hybrid reduces scrolling for stats but adds layout complexity; grouped keeps implementation simpler.
Skipping adversarial Codex review vs blocking on it: proceeding without review saves time given the spec is a straightforward UI enhancement with no new data pipelines.
codebase_patterns: Detail pane boxes are rendered as bordered lipgloss boxes with uppercase labels.
Sub-section headers use dim uppercase labels inside boxes.
Evidence items are rendered as indented lines with a ↳ prefix.
Friction rendering is gated on HasSummary field.
Spec files go in docs/superpowers/specs/ with date-prefixed filenames.
Plan files go in docs/superpowers/plans/ with date-prefixed filenames.
